source: If Hamlet and Claudius are the ones with the problem, why must I be asked to leave the castle? I've done nothing wrong.
It's simply the way things are, my dear.
Regardless, I don't believe there's an immediate danger to you. Still, stay far from Hamlet until we can find somewhere to place you in Copenhagen. Yes?
Furthermore, as I mentioned before, I overheard... a conversation... implying that the King may have wanted me dead.
Laertes heard it too.
Now that he's passed, of course, the threat seems far diminished.
Er... what makes you say that, dearest?
It's... it's a... I have a sense I've experienced it before. I know how insane it sounds, but... it's true, I promise.
Dearest, have you been sleeping well?
No, I haven't—but that's not the reason for this, Father.
And Hamlet, has he been giving you trouble?
A little more than usual—Father, listen. I'm telling the truth!
Love. You're worrying me.
If your brother were here, he'd only indulge you in this. Luckily for us both, he isn't.
(He's always taken care of me when I've been in trouble before.)
I assure you it will be fine. But I've got court affairs to attend to, and Laertes is preparing to leave from the docks as we speak.
Is this why Laertes cancelled his trip? Because of this?
Not to mention, with the King frightened of a potential spy in his court—a rumor like this could be quite dangerous.
Tell the good Bernardo of your concerns, if they run so deep.
Someone is trying to threaten my life.
What? Who?
I don't know. But they are.
How do you know?
I don't have proof, but—I—I let's say I had an unnerving experience which made me doubt my safety.
I can add more patrols to the night's watch, if you're worried. But Ophelia, you're a noblewoman of the court, and relatively unthreatening. Who would want you dead?
Bernardo, please—haven't we known each other long enough for you to believe me?
Well, if it will bring you comfort... you should know I've been asked by the King to meet with anyone deemed suspicious or threatening to the throne.
Well, if it will bring you comfort... before he passed, His Majesty requested I meet with anyone deemed suspicious or threatening to the throne.
I intend to continue that mission, even now.
If you sense someone's acting strangely, ask them to meet with me. I'll speak with them further and identify whether or not they're a danger to you.
It need not take the form of some solemn meeting. I'll keep it to a lightweight chat of sorts.
My eternal thanks, Bernardo. That's all I wanted.
Someone is trying to kill me off. But I don't know who.
Oh! I love a good thriller. I'll play your sidekick.
Horatio, I'm not trying to be funny.
Oh. Er, I thought we were sort of... play-acting. Really? Whoever would want to kill you?
No letter with a mysterious wax seal? No threatening silhouettes outside your bedroom door?
Well, there was someone...
Did you catch what they looked like?
No. And even if I did, I've no idea if it was someone I knew or a stranger.
Well, that does it, then. You'll just have to wait for this antagonist to make another appearance.
If they do, surely Bernardo can dispatch them with one swing of the sword, right?
In fact, you should go tell Bernardo of this. Watch him turn white as a sheet. He takes these sorts of things so seriously. Bless him.
Someone is trying to kill me off. Maybe you'll believe me.
Is there a punchline here? This must be a joke, right?
No. Someone wants me dead.
Well, that's melodramatic.
It's sort of a... premonition, really. But I swear, it's true.
You mentioned earlier that you thought the King might be behind this.
If he were after your life, how would you know?
Someone physically threatened me. Let's keep it at that.
They-- they did?
No. That's impossible.
I see through this. You're trying to persuade me to play into this little game, then set me up to look like a fool.
Go away.
I've heard of things like this before.
You have?
Yes. It's a form of insanity that comes on to women during times of intense pressure.
Ah. Hysteria! That's the word.
I'm not hysterical, Brit. I'm right. I know I am.
I don't know why I thought you would help me.
Someone is trying to kill me off.
Someone is trying to kill all of us off! His name is Death, and he comes for us all in time!
I lived through plague. Don't tell me about death, girl!
We must outrun it all our short lives!
Irma, I'm being earnest. I'm afraid for my life. Can you help me?
Oh. Apologies, Fräulein. W-well, ah, have you spoken to Guard Captain Bernardo?
No woman can be afraid with a man twice her size at her side.
I haven't got time for your fanciful daydreams, Ophelia.
When you were a child, I entertained them. Now that I'm King, I don't have time to entertain anyone.
If you've a legitimate security concern, please report it to Bernardo.
Where is your father? He ought to mind you more closely, or take you to a doctor.
Oh, Ophelia.
I can understand that with your father's death, much has changed.
That brother of yours ought to watch out for you.
And-- with young Laertes gone, I expect your heart is heavy right now.
I find myself deeply concerned for your well-being, indeed. Just not for the reasons you propose.
Someone's after my life. Do you know who might want me dead?
You? Certainly not. But...
If my plot to fake my own death works as nicely as I think it will, perhaps you ought to give it a try!
At least if you died, people would probably be upset, right?
That... doesn't make me feel better, Guilda.
Oh, dear. I suppose that is rather harrowing.
Well, have you gravely offended anyone as of late?
Are you pregnant with anyone's illegitimate child?
N-not to my knowledge.
Hopped into bed with anyone's husband? Or wife, for that matter?
Again, no to both.
Then I am pleased to announce that all possible reasons for your demise have been exhausted.
Go, and live without fear!
I feel as though time is repeating itself for me, over and over again.
Just as it was for my father...
There are so many things I don't understand about the universe.
I feel as though the fabric of things has been rended in two.
And I am falling through the hole in the center...
The last few hours have been enormously eventful for this dull place.
Rest a while, if you can. I've been sleeping whenever I have a moment. It will help settle the strangeness, I think.
Yes, life in this castle does seem to drone on, ever repeating...
Really repeating, Hamlet.
You know, you really have gotten odd—
All these things you're saying about murdering and time and—
And they say I'm the mad one.
Why is time repeating?
You can end this game any time you like, my dear.
Being obstinate will merely delay the inevitable.
...You know, Quince. Every time you say that, I feel the strength to search a little longer.
The more you try to break my spirit... the longer this world will be drawn out.
I operate on the scale of centuries. Not days. Let's chat again in a hundred years of this, shall we?
I am, after all, an exceedingly patient man.
And if one loves a good story, one must adopt a certain level of patience. The good ones are... slow burns.
Why do you think time is repeating?
Perhaps there's something I haven't done. Perhaps I'm being punished by... by God, or something.
They say spirits roam the earth until they find their final purpose...
What rubbish. No, that's not it at all.
This world is without purpose, divine or otherwise. There is only the meaning you make for yourself.
After all, that person is still coming to kill you, aren't they?
If other corpses could have another chance at life, they'd spend less time on philosophy than you are, I'm certain.
Why don't you find a way to prevent your death?
After all, the Prince of Norway himself has found a way to Elsinore's doorstep.
If all citizens of conquered countries could have another chance at deposing such coups... they'd be blindingly grateful.
After all, the spirit of King Hamlet still lingers within these walls.
Haven't you found a way to free him yet, or have you spent all your time in crisis?
Certainly you've heard Hamlet saw the ghost of his father.
Mightn't that be the source of his madness, from which your own father lost his life?
A good daughter might be more motivated to pursue that thread and spend less time on philosophy.
The two of us are outside the flow of all time, right?
Yes. In a way, it is peaceful.
All suffering is, in one way or another, caused by death, or the fear of it...
Now that fear is removed forever, replaced by an equally-deep boredom.
Even still, this boredom is refreshing at the moment, though I anticipate it, too, will grow old.
And when it does... well.
To divest oneself of the fear of death, one need only give into it.
How does one divest oneself of eternal boredom?
I suppose you'd start acting strangely. Doing all sorts of things to pass the time.
Indeed. A most frightening prospect.
I don't know how or why, but I've lived through this same day once before, as though time is repeating.
Oh, Ophelia. You've been through so much in such a short time. No wonder you feel strangely.
Perhaps you've been ill and are only just noticing it?
When the color comes over me, I feel faint as well, and strange, as though time is passing slowly and yet quickly...
No, it's not like sickness, it's—it's real.
Oh, dear. Ophelia... hrm.
You've been saying the strangest things lately. Murders, repeating time...
Have a lie down, have a bit of wine, and come back later, why don't you? I'm certain you'll feel good as new.
I feel as though time is repeating itself somehow.
Time... time is going back and forth in a strange way.
Oh hell, sister. Have you been drinking?
No! I'm telling the truth!
I don't know how or why, but I've lived through this same day before.
It's odd, I know. But it feels as though time is...
It seems it's a common madness in this castle.
And now it's gotten into your bones.
Well, I won't let you go the way they did.
Who? Who is 'they?'
I love you, dearest. Get some rest.
